correctness.rationale: The randomly marked cyclic gaps have exchangeable Dirichlet(1,...,1) density. Their rank permutation is uniform and independent of sorted gap lengths. Mutual neighbor pairs are cyclic local minima, a rank-measurable count; at radius r, component count equals max(1, number of gaps>r), a sorted-value measurable process. Independence follows for all radii jointly. Exact local valley indicator covariance gives variance 2n/45 for n>=5 and explicit small n cases. Independent exact permutation checker passed.

originality.rationale: The independence separates a cyclic-rank statistic from all sorted-gap statistics, in particular the entire connected-component count process. The rank-order-statistic identity is classical and not claimed new. Closest identified prior results concern marginal connected-component distributions, reciprocal pair means, or dependence with isolated-vertex count, none of which implies independence from the all-radius count process. Older nearest-neighbor literature is an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: Classical order-statistic/rank independence is an elementary underlying theorem; independent scholarly judgment could consider its geometric specialization routine.

value.rationale: This process-level exact independence separates local reciprocal nearest-neighbor motifs from multiscale global connectivity across every threshold, giving unconditional=conditional laws even under observations of the entire connectivity curve. The contrast with non-independent isolated-vertex counts is a motivated structural distinction in geometric networks; explicit variance covers the finite model and shows the rank statistic is nondegenerate at n>=4.
